card.situation:
Solicitation for tree and vegetation trimming, mulching, and clearing services at Marais des Cygnes National Wildlife Refuge in Kansas (trails and levees), set aside for Total Small Business, NAICS 561730, with a 12-month period of performance.
Reached the owner because Red Cedar's NAICS 561730 matches exactly and the firm holds Total Small Business eligibility, but the scope requires specialized forestry and wildland fire safety capabilities not documented in the firm profile.
reasons_for: NAICS 561730 is an exact match and Total Small Business set-aside eligibility is confirmed, making Red Cedar administratively eligible to compete [profile: WOSB/EDWOSB/SBA set-aside eligibility].
OSHA 30 supervisors and a CMMS-logged QC inspection program provide a credible foundation for the daily tailgate safety briefing requirement [3d699772-cae04cc8-p2-1b4ea67b].

Federal coordination experience across GSA, DoD, and VA demonstrates the administrative and compliance readiness needed for amendment acknowledgment, IPP invoicing, SAM rerepresentations, and records retention [3d699772-8ad8ca08-p2-366c1aa4].
reasons_against: The firm has no documented chainsaw, mulcher, chipper, or heavy forestry equipment capability, leaving the core technical scope entirely unmet [3d699772-cae04cc8-p2-0f306e34].

Four wildland fire safety requirements — spark arrestors, daily fire-risk inspections, suppression tools on equipment, and end-of-day fire watch — are all gaps with zero supporting evidence in the firm profile [3d699772-cae04cc8-p2-55c1d9c1; 3d699772-cae04cc8-p2-10bf6b5f; 3d699772-cae04cc8-p3-3afe0ad6].

Only one marginally relevant past-performance record exists (grounds maintenance, Tinker AFB), making it effectively impossible to submit the required two to three qualifying vegetation trimming/clearing examples without risking a non-responsive determination [3d699772-79173c4f-p3-c07b2f48].

drafts.capability_statement:
Red Cedar Facility Services is a Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB/EDWOSB) registered under NAICS 561730 (Landscaping Services) and fully eligible to compete under this Total Small Business set-aside.

Red Cedar brings federal grounds maintenance experience including mowing, trimming, and landscaping services performed at Tinker Air Force Base, demonstrating the ability to execute recurring exterior maintenance work on active federal installations under agency oversight and coordination requirements.

Our supervisory staff hold OSHA 30 certifications, supporting the daily tailgate safety briefing requirement and the safe equipment operation standards specified in this solicitation. We maintain a CMMS-based quality control and inspection program that documents daily work activities, supports records retention, and provides audit-ready documentation consistent with FAR requirements.

Red Cedar holds active federal contracts with GSA Region 7, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Veterans Affairs, demonstrating sustained compliance with federal administrative requirements including SAM registration, IPP invoicing, amendment acknowledgment, and FAR clause adherence.

We are registered and current in SAM.gov, carry required federal liability coverage, and participate in E-Verify. Our coordination experience across multiple federal agencies supports the access, closure, and work-sequencing coordination required by the refuge manager on this contract.

Red Cedar is actively assessing equipment and teaming resources to address the specialized vegetation clearing, mulching, and wildland fire safety requirements of this solicitation and welcomes the opportunity to discuss our approach with the contracting officer.

Point of Contact: [Owner Name] | [Phone] | [Email]
questions_for_co: Treatment types and project map (req 3d699772-cae04cc8-p1-ddc2e6db): Could the government provide the project map and a description of the specific treatment types (e.g., selective clearing, full clearing, mulching-only zones) prior to the proposal due date so offerors can accurately scope equipment, labor, and acreage estimates?

Chainsaw and heavy equipment operator qualifications (req 3d699772-cae04cc8-p2-0f306e34): Does the government require specific certifications or training records for chainsaw and heavy-equipment operators (e.g., manufacturer training, state licensing, or agency-specific qualification), or is demonstrated experience and OSHA-compliant safe operating procedures sufficient?

Spark arrestor and fire-risk inspection documentation (req 3d699772-cae04cc8-p2-55c1d9c1): Must spark arrestor compliance and daily fire-risk inspection records be submitted to the refuge manager on a set schedule, and does the government have a preferred form or log format for this documentation?

Fire suppression equipment standards (req 3d699772-cae04cc8-p2-10bf6b5f): Are there specific capacity or type requirements for fire extinguishers, water packs, and suppression tools that must be maintained on each piece of equipment, or does the contractor have discretion to determine appropriate quantities based on equipment type and work area?

End-of-day fire watch and high-risk period definition (req 3d699772-cae04cc8-p3-3afe0ad6): How does the refuge manager define and communicate 'high-risk periods' requiring end-of-day fire watch — for example, by fire weather index, wind speed, or a standing seasonal calendar — and what is the minimum duration of the required fire watch?

Wet-condition stop-work and erosion control protocols (reqs 3d699772-cae04cc8-p2-f160ce5d and 3d699772-e668cb28-p2-475b8286): When the refuge manager directs a work pause due to wet conditions, is the contractor expected to demobilize equipment from the site or simply halt operations in place, and are there specific erosion-control best management practices (e.g., matting, designated access routes) the contractor must follow in soft or wet areas?
